title: Temperature in Softmax Distillation

paper.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

hook: How does a neural network reveal its 'dark knowledge'? By softening its softmax outputs with a temperature parameter. Explore how temperature controls the softness of a probability distribution.

equation.caption: Softmax with temperature T. Higher T produces a softer distribution.

steps: Given logits \(z_i\) and temperature \(T\), compute \(\exp(z_i/T)\) for each class.
Divide each exponential by the sum: \(p_i = \exp(z_i/T) / S\).

explorations.title: Effect of high temperature
explorations.predict: What happens to the probabilities when T is very large?
explorations.observe: The probabilities become nearly uniform (all close to 0.25).
explorations.why: As T → ∞, z_i/T → 0, so exp(z_i/T) → 1 for all i, making p_i → 1/K.

explorations.title: Effect of low temperature
explorations.predict: What happens when T is very small?
explorations.observe: The largest logit dominates; its probability approaches 1.
explorations.why: As T → 0, differences in z_i/T are amplified, so the softmax approaches a one-hot distribution at the maximum logit.

limitation: This demonstration uses a fixed set of logits and does not show how temperature affects the training of a distilled model, where the student is trained on the soft targets produced by the teacher.
misconception: Temperature is not a parameter of the softmax function itself; it is a hyperparameter that controls the softness of the output distribution. It does not change the ranking of the logits.

claims.text: Softmax with temperature T is defined as p_i = exp(z_i/T) / sum_j exp(z_j/T).
As T approaches infinity, the softmax distribution approaches the uniform distribution.
As T approaches 0, the softmax distribution approaches a one-hot distribution at the maximum logit.
In our toy setup, we use 4 logits and allow the user to adjust them and T to see the effect on probabilities.

outcomes.outcome: Explain how temperature T affects the softmax distribution.
Recognize that high T leads to a softer distribution and low T to a sharper one.
